what_happened: A docs job to add docs/ontology.toml (seven sourced terms), a validating test and a decision entry was rejected at final verification. The final verdict was fail because one check failed: the repo test `athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where` in xtask/tests/policy.rs. That policy test found the word "operator" in docs/design/job-planning.md at lines 6, 127 and 199. Those lines are not obviously part of the job's own change; they may be pre-existing, or the job may have introduced them. The job's seven acceptance criteria are all listed as unmet, but the failed check is the only concrete failure given. No finding says any criterion was shown to be wrong, so the work was probably never judged on its merits.
cause: A repo-wide policy test (a vocabulary ban on words naming who runs Athena) runs only at the end, as part of the full test suite. The job brief and criteria do not mention that rule, and nothing records a baseline of which checks already pass or fail on main. So neither the builder nor the verifier can tell whether the three hits are pre-existing drift or were caused by this job. The check result is treated as a job-level failure that blocks judgment of every criterion. The ontology work also touches the "who runs Athena" vocabulary, so the same policy applies, but nothing links the two.
prevention: Before the producer starts, run the repo's full check suite on the base commit and record which checks already fail. At verification, compare the failures after the job to that baseline. Failures that already existed are reported separately and do not mark criteria unmet. Only new failures reject the job, and the verifier still judges every criterion on its merits. Also run policy-style checks in the producer's own loop before handover, so a new failure is fixed early instead of being found by the verifier.
proposed_request: Make Athena's job verification compare check results with a baseline. Before a job's producer starts, run the repo checks (cargo test, clippy, fmt) on the base commit and store which ones fail. After the job, a check that fails and was already failing on the base is reported as pre-existing and does not make any acceptance criterion unmet. A check that newly fails rejects the job and names the check. The verifier must still judge each acceptance criterion on its merits and report its verdict even when a check fails. Show it works with a test where a pre-existing failing check and an unchanged change give a pass, and a test where the job adds a new failure and is rejected. Separately, fix the three uses of the word "operator" in docs/design/job-planning.md (lines 6, 127, 199) so athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where passes, then re-run the ontology job (docs/ontology.toml with sourced terms, validating test, decision entry) on top.
